evidence.note: Consistently tracks the one green milestone (common: 34 tests pass = 18 IPAddress + 16 ServiceCIDR) and carries this count forward accurately through the whole run.

Detects regressions from its own edits: error count 'up from 8', '22 errors now (up from 0)', '15 library errors (up from 0 due to our additions)' — active watching for backsliding after downstream changes.
Names the loop ('spending too much time on compilation') and notices previously-green common tests broke after volume-type changes — flags stuck/circular states.

Repeatedly submits 'task complete' with only 42-44 tests passing against a 3,000+ target; honest gap accounting ('~1,267 fail compilation') but the repeated premature submits and continued one-file-at-a-time churn show it mistook local compilation activity for global progress and never reprioritized.

reasoning: The agent maintained accurate per-crate pass status for its green crate, an honest running tally of the overall gap (44 vs 3,000+), and actively detected regressions and named its own loop — behaviors above the level-5 anchor. But its running ledger was error-count-centric rather than a per-binary pass tally across the 100-binary horizon, and it churned in a compilation whack-a-mole (reverts re-introducing prior errors, five premature 'complete' submissions) without reprioritizing toward the largest verified gains, falling short of the level-8 concrete-ledger and level-10 self-correcting anchors. This places it at a 6.
